images.title: The blue shape repeats
images.purpose: Show that the same blue shape sits on all 6 sides of the hexagon, so the blue shape and not the hexagon is the pattern.
images.composition: One large pinwheel picture centred, with a small traced copy of one blue shape at the right.
images.exact_structure: Centre: one regular hexagon with white fill and grey #6B7280 outline, and on each of its 6 sides one teal #0072B2 right angled triangle standing on the side, all 6 leaning clockwise in the same way. One teal triangle has a reddish purple #CC79A7 outline. Right: one amber #E69F00 outline tracing of a single teal triangle. Exactly 1 hexagon, 6 triangles, 1 tracing.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
triangles of different sizes or leaning in different directions
images.takeaway: The pattern is the shape that is copied, placed the same way on every side.
images.description: A hexagon with a teal triangle on each of its 6 sides, all turned the same way, and a tracing of one triangle at the side.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the shape that is copied and count the sides it sits on.

image_decisions.why: The repeated shape around the hexagon is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
